scope: Fresh corrected-domain optimized physical oracle and all-three selection reduction checks, followed by separate instrumented execution accounting. No primary timing samples.

same_artifact_policy.ordinary: All three reduction selections use one identical copied native-enabled Rust library and one identical C++ runner. The physical oracle uses that same Rust library, with a separate C++ oracle driver.
same_artifact_policy.execution: All three selections use one identical copied instrumented library/runner, distinct from ordinary primary timing artifacts.

frozen_master_policy: Per-process captures of the same ordered request union/backend policy, original and Rust sharing one frozen handle within each process. The physical oracle checks all three selections against literally one union/handle.
callback_work_policy: Identical PolynomialNumerator provider and equal sampled callback row counts. Requested expansion heads/depths can differ between reducers; equal rows do not mean equal callback arithmetic. Original Ninja reduces the swapped bubble expansion depth, whereas this Rust baseline requests full depth for both orientations.

corrected_domain_regression.result: At the retained extreme finite correction input, native f64 now exposes nonfinite failure instead of incorrect finite zero. Float256 resolves the finite answer; this guard does not restore f64 arithmetic accuracy.

coverage.selection_scope: Setup-only partial catalog; unused stages need not execute. Numerator, geometry and masters are independent.
Setup-only partial catalog; unused stages need not execute. Numerator, geometry and masters are independent.
Setup-only partial catalog; unused stages need not execute. Numerator, geometry and masters are independent.

oracle.precision_oracle_boundary: Float256 exactly promotes binary64 physical component inputs after wavefunction evaluation; this checks coefficient arithmetic, not high-precision physical wavefunctions.

accounting.unit: integer nanoseconds from monotonic clocks, calls and evaluated rows
accounting.nesting: Shared backend execution is nested in shared ABI spans; Rust preparation provider is nested in full C++ preparation. Additive accounting subtracts each nested span once; numerator and full preparation are disjoint from masters.
accounting.master_backend_scope: Actual provider execution, including its ordinary validation/conversion and expression arithmetic; no result-cache hits. Original rank2/3 bubbles are grouped calls, not fabricated individual family timings. Scale initialization is separate and retained in remainder.
accounting.master_lookup_transport_scope: Rust shared-master ABI, decoding, exact-key lookup, output copying and validation, excluding its nested backend. Caller-side C++/Rust packing remains in remainder.
accounting.remainder_scope: Core reduction, contraction, caller-side staging/transport, unassigned initialization and instrumentation overhead; not a pure arithmetic measurement.

numerator_provider.reduction_callbacks: Same PolynomialNumerator<f64> and generic Symbolica batched interpreter for direct/Mu/T3/T2; callbacks are not JIT compiled

limitations: Busy shared host; no performance acceptance or primary timing samples.
Single-call instrumented records are attribution diagnostics, not paired uninstrumented benchmark samples.
Native catalog covers two denominator and three correction/source-projection families; geometry and remaining reduction/integration/accumulation remain interpreted.
The same numerator provider still interprets direct/Mu/T3/T2 callbacks. SymJIT compiles coefficient heads only.
Frozen lookup/transport remains included in reduction controls, but actual master backend execution is structurally zero.
Real f64 overflow remains a numerical failure; no silent rescue or domain expansion is claimed.
Physical Float256 oracle promotes represented binary64 component inputs; no high-precision wavefunction oracle.
